Up 3 in the last 12 seconds, should the leader foul or defend?
rows.a: Foul. The leader wins 93.6% of the time fouling and 92.4% defending, +2.8 points at equal time (CI +0.8 to +4.6).

rows.t: Does a timeout before a late free throw make the shooter miss?
rows.a: Icing doesn't work. Iced shooters were +2.3 points better than un-iced shooters, relative to their own FT% (CI +0.0 to +4.6).

rows.t: How do the in-season award odds (NBA, NFL, NHL, CFB) compare with traded prices?
rows.a: The market is far ahead. Winner log loss was 2.34 for the model and 1.22 for Polymarket on the 2025-26 races.

rows.t: Up 3 in the last 12 seconds, should the leader foul or defend?
rows.a: There is no clear edge. The leader wins 92.7% of the time fouling and 91.4% defending, +2.3 points at equal time (CI -2.4 to +6.4).

rows.t: Does a timeout stop an opponent run?
rows.a: No. After a run of 8+ points, a timeout nets -0.31 points over the next 2:00 compared to playing on (CI -0.40 to -0.23).

rows.t: With 25-40 seconds left in a quarter, does a quick shot for a 2-for-1 pay?
rows.a: Yes. A quick shot nets +0.33 points per quarter-end compared to a full possession (CI +0.26 to +0.39).

rows.t: How much does an equipment gap change round win chances on CT and T?
rows.a: Full buy against full buy, the CT side wins 51.7%. At equal dollar value the CT side wins 48.5%, and an eco beats a full buy 5.6% of the time.

rows.t: Does a losing streak hurt the next round beyond economy (the no-timeout baseline)?
rows.a: There is no tilt. After 3+ straight losses a team wins +0.9 points more than an economy and score model expects.

rows.t: After losing the pistol round, should the team save or buy on round 2?
rows.a: Buying on round 2 is worth +26.8 points in round 2 and -16.5 points in round 3. The map win is -0.8 points, which isn't different from 0.

rows.t: How much is the first pistol round worth, and does the side matter?
rows.a: The winner of the first pistol takes the map 59.5% of the time, 57.1% from the CT side and 61.9% from the T side.

rows.t: Do intentional walks gain win probability for the defense?
rows.a: Mostly no. With a runner on 2nd and 1 out, the IBB costs the defense 2.0 points of win probability. In the other states there is no gain I can tell apart from 0.

rows.t: Do sacrifice-bunt tries with nobody out gain win probability?
rows.a: No. A bunt try costs 0.3 to 0.9 points of win probability compared to swinging, and up to 1.9 late and close.

rows.t: After the 2023 base and pickoff rules, do runners still steal too little?
rows.a: Slightly. Steals of 2nd succeed 75.9% of the time against a 71.7% break-even, worth +2.6 runs per team-season. With 1 out there is no edge.

rows.t: Does the times-through-the-order penalty justify pulling starters before the 3rd time?
rows.a: For an average starter, yes. The 3rd time through is +.022 wOBA over the 1st for the same pitcher, .339 against .323 for relievers.

rows.t: Down 14 in the 4th, should a team go for two after the first touchdown?
rows.a: Yes. Given two TDs and a stop, going for 2 first wins 59% of the time, against 47% for kicking. Teams went for 2 54% of the time in 2025-26.

rows.t: When going for it on 4th down gains win probability, how often do NFL teams go?
rows.a: In states where going gains 1+ point of WP, teams went 25% of the time in 2015-16 and 45% in 2024-25.

rows.t: How well does NFL WAR rank the first-team All-Pros at each position?
rows.a: AUC is .92+ at QB, WR, TE, DL, LB and DB, 0.82 on the offensive line and 0.75 at running back.

rows.t: Do surprise onside kicks get recovered more than expected late-game onside kicks?
rows.a: Yes, 25% against 9% (2015-23), but that is below the ~32% break-even for an early onside. Net WPA isn't different from zero.

rows.t: On 3rd or 4th and 1, does the QB sneak convert more often than other plays?
rows.a: Yes. Sneaks convert 82% of the time, other runs 69% and passes 56%. The sneak share of these plays went from 8% in 2015 to 14% in 2025.

rows.t: Is a two-point try worth more than an extra point on average?
rows.a: There is no clear edge. A 2-pt try scores 0.96 points per try and an XP scores 0.94, a difference of +0.02 (-0.03 to +0.07).

rows.t: When should a trailing team pull its goalie?
rows.a: Pull at 3:18 down one and at 6:27 down two. Teams pull at 1:52 and 2:39.

rows.t: Should a team down one late pull its goalie on a power play?
rows.a: Yes, with 3:00 or less left. 6v4 adds 8 points of tie chance at 2:00. Past 4:00 the gain isn't clear.

rows.t: Do teams score more or less in the minutes after a goal?
rows.a: There is no momentum swing. The team that just conceded scores at 0.95x its baseline in the next 10 min, and the scorer at 1.06x. The restart dips the first 3 min.

rows.t: When do teams make their first sub by score state, and does an early first sub pay off?
rows.a: Trailing teams make their first sub by 60', and level and leading teams by 65'. A first sub before 60' adds +0.04 of xG difference, and I found no effect on goals.

rows.t: Does a team leading by one goal lose the xG battle late, and does it cost points?
rows.a: Yes, after 75'. Its xG share is 46% against an expected 53%. That costs 0.05 xPts from 75', but the actual points held.

rows.t: Do players drop serve more often right after breaking?
rows.a: No. For the same player and match, the hold rate after breaking is +0.7 points (men) and +0.5 (women) higher than after the opponent holds.

rows.t: Should players hit a first serve on second serve?
rows.a: No. 1 of 188 men and 0 of 112 women gain with a CI above 0. The median player loses 6.8 points per 100 (men) and 5.3 (women).

rows.t: Do first serves wide, body and T win at equal rates, as mixed-strategy theory predicts?
rows.a: Wide and T do, within 1 point for the same server. Body doesn't. It is 4.2 points lower for men and 4.1 for women.
